body: I was planning on doing a couple of the "common parser idioms", but actually replacing those terms is more work than I thought.
(If we had rewrapping software this would be a lot easier by the way. Maybe we should give that another thought.)

LGTM, merge at will, although I'd kind of prefer doing more at once. That would minimize the re-wrapping and it seems a bit strange that in the same sentence "ASCII whitespace" and "ASCII digits" go to different specs.

> If we had rewrapping software this would be a lot easier by the way. Maybe we should give that another thought.

Give this a shot: https://jsbin.com/maferi
Oh yeah, this is just how far I got. Feel free to add or I will get back to it Monday.
I think I'm okay with merging this now.
LGTM assuming it builds.

Are these character classes plural or singular or both? E.g.

> The attribute value can remain unquoted if it doesn't contain ASCII whitespace or any of ...

could theoretically be "ASCII whitespaces". That one sounds weird, but on the other hand

> expressed in hexadecimal using ASCII hex digit upper

sounds a bit strange and as if it should be "ASCII hex digit uppers" (or, "ASCII upper hex digits").

Maybe we just declare that you always use the singular form? If so it might be worth adding a note to infra about that.
Hmm, I guess I don't really know what would be good.

I guess this is fine for now, unless you want to rearrange all the infra terms to have their nouns at the end first (i.e. ASCII hex digit upper -> ASCII upper hex digit etc.) so that we can have more flexibility later.

Sigh. I'm feeling particularly indecisive. We do use both "ASCII digit" and "ASCII digits".

Looking through the Infra Standard:

* ASCII tab or newline: add ASCII tabs or newlines?
* ASCII whitespace: denote as mass noun
* C0 control or space: add C0 controls or spaces?
* ASCII hex digit upper/lower: denote as mass noun
* ASCII alpha upper/lower: denote as mass noun
* ASCII alpha: denote as mass noun
* ASCII alphanumeric: denote as mass noun

Defining everything as singular terms seems OK to me, and putting the word that could possibly be pluralized last allows specs (that use bikeshed) to use the plural form if that happens to read better.
@zcorpan so you want to adjust the terms first?
Yeah.

FWIW, I do think we should try to use the terms consistently. So if we are going to allow pluralized forms, we should use them where we think it makes sense. I don't think it makes sense for ASCII whitespace and ASCII alpha* (even if specific variants are renamed to ASCII upper/lower alpha).
Proposed the change to Infra. Once that lands the work here can continue.
This should be all good now.
@domenic Infra explicitly calls out "alpha" and "alphanumeric" as mass nouns.

Hmm, OK. Somehow I missed that. I don't think they should be mass nouns, but on the other hand maybe we should just get this merged...

The note starting "Space characters before the html element" should probably be converted to use ASCII whitespace, I think?
I'm with Domenic - they're not mass nouns in my ideolect, and I don't think they are in most people's.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphanumeric seems to use it as mass noun. "Alpha" the way we use it is novel so can go either way. I'll have a look at the "Space characters" thing.

> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphanumeric seems to use it as mass noun.

I think it only uses it as an adjective. If you don't object too strongly, I think it'd be best to update these to use "s" pluralizations.
Meh, feel free to take over or I'll get to it in 2017.

The Wikipedia article is actually inconsistent, with both

> various subsets of the alphanumeric were adopted

and

> For alphanumerics that are frequently handwritten

The first stands out as immediately wrong to me.
